prompt: What does a tester doubt, in this lesson’s sense of systematic doubt?

choices.text: Nothing until a test has failed
choices.why: The doubt comes before the failure; it is what finds it.

choices.text: The product owner’s priorities for the sprint
choices.why: Priorities are hers to set; the doubt is about what has been checked.

choices.text: Claims about the software
choices.why: Right: "it works" is a claim about the inputs tried.

choices.text: The competence of the developers who wrote it
choices.why: That is suspicion, and it makes developers stop showing their work early.

prompt: Which question asks what is known rather than asking somebody to defend themselves?
hint: One question everybody can help answer.

choices.text: Did you make a mistake?
choices.why: That asks a person to defend themselves.

choices.text: Why did you not test this properly before handing it over?
choices.why: Blame dressed as a question.

choices.text: Who reviewed it?
choices.why: A name, not a fact about the software.

choices.text: What has this been checked against, and what has not?
choices.why: Right: it is about evidence, not about a person.

prompt: Why does a second person find defects the author missed, according to this lesson?

choices.text: Developers are careless
choices.why: Rafael’s claim was honest; the bias is human, not careless.

choices.text: A second person runs more tests in total, and more tests always find more defects
choices.why: It is which inputs are chosen, not how many.

choices.text: Distance: they do not believe it yet
choices.why: Right: the author chooses inputs they expect to pass.

choices.text: Testers are better at reading code than developers
choices.why: The lesson says it is not skill: the same tester has the same blind spot on their own work.

prompt: Which of these is a hypothesis in the lesson’s sense?
hint: It must be capable of being wrong.

choices.text: A time written without a leading zero is charged as evening
choices.why: Right: one run of `09:30` against `9:30` can refute it.

choices.text: The shop has some kind of problem with the session times on its pages
choices.why: No run could refute it, so it is not a hypothesis.

choices.text: Something is wrong on Sundays, probably
choices.why: Vague, and hedged: nothing would count against it.

choices.text: Rafael’s code has a bug somewhere in the part that handles times
choices.why: About a person and unfalsifiable as stated.

prompt: Match each word to what it was in the Sunday investigation.
hint: The table in the first section.

pairs.right: the time reached the rule in a form it does not handle
run `9:30` and `09:30` for the same adult

prompt: How many reais did the website overcharge the family of four?
R$ 108,00 is two times R$ 36,00 plus two times R$ 18,00. What did that arithmetic rule out before any run?
hint: The children were charged half of something.

choices.text: The children’s discount
choices.why: Right: half of the evening price is a working discount on the wrong session price.

choices.text: A problem with the session price
choices.why: That is what it pointed at, not what it ruled out.

choices.text: The possibility that the family was wrong
choices.why: The order record ruled that out, not the arithmetic.

choices.text: Nothing: arithmetic is not evidence
choices.why: The lesson says the arithmetic is evidence too.

prompt: Why did Lia list four hypotheses before testing any of them?
hint: What happens when you test the first idea and it looks plausible?

choices.text: To be able to blame the right person
choices.why: None of the hypotheses is about a person.

choices.text: Because running the program is expensive and she wanted to run it only once, at the end
choices.why: Runs are cheap; listing first is about not stopping too early.

choices.text: The first idea that fits tempts you to stop
choices.why: Right: confirmation bias, from the tester’s side.

choices.text: Four is the number a defect report requires
choices.why: There is no such number.

prompt: Of several hypotheses, which should be tested first?
hint: Cost and how much it rules out.

choices.text: The last one on the list
choices.why: Order of writing decides nothing.

choices.text: Cheapest, ruling out most
choices.why: Right: the family’s order record settled the fourth for nothing.

choices.text: The most likely one, whatever it costs to check
choices.why: Likelihood matters, and so does cost; the lesson weighs both.

choices.text: The one the developer suggests
choices.why: Lia had not told Rafael anything yet.

prompt: Which run ruled out Sunday as the cause?
hint: An adult, on a Sunday, in the afternoon.

choices.text: Re-running the family’s purchase
choices.why: It confirms the complaint and separates nothing.

choices.text: The adult at 15:00 on Sunday
choices.why: Right: a Sunday matinée charged as a matinée.

choices.text: `python tickets.py 35 no sun 9:30`
choices.why: That run shows the defect; it does not separate Sunday from the time.

choices.text: `python tickets.py 35 no wed 20:00`
choices.why: A Wednesday says nothing about Sunday.

prompt: `9:30` costs R$ 36,00 and `09:30` costs R$ 28,00. What does that separate?

choices.text: How the time is written, from the hour
choices.why: Right: the same moment gives two prices.

choices.text: Sunday from the other days of the week
choices.why: Both runs are on Sunday.

choices.text: Adults from children
choices.why: Both are the same adult.

choices.text: The website from the program
choices.why: Both runs are the program.

prompt: `tickets.py` compares the session time as ___, character by character, so "9:30" sorts after "17:00".
hint: Not as a time of day.

prompt: The defect was in `tickets.py` from the first day. Why did nobody see it until the Sunday?
hint: What shape did every earlier time have?

choices.text: No session time before had a single digit before the colon
choices.why: Right: no input had ever been of the shape that reaches the defect.

choices.text: It was introduced on the Saturday by a change Rafael made
choices.why: The line was the same from the start.

choices.text: A Python update changed the way two pieces of text are compared
choices.why: Text has compared that way all along.

choices.text: Nobody had tested on a Sunday
choices.why: Sunday is not the cause; the afternoon run showed it.

prompt: What does the lesson say is wrong with "change something, try again, repeat until it goes away"?

choices.text: It is only allowed for developers
choices.why: Nothing about permission.

choices.text: No cause, no evidence
choices.why: Right: a problem that vanishes unexplained comes back.

choices.text: It never finds a fix
choices.why: It does find one, sometimes.

choices.text: It takes more commands than the method does
choices.why: The objection is what it leaves behind, not the count.

prompt: What makes a reproduction good, by this lesson’s test?
hint: Somebody who never heard of the problem.

choices.text: It includes a fix
choices.why: The fix is the developer’s next step.

choices.text: A newcomer runs it and sees the defect without asking you
choices.why: Right: Rafael could, with two commands.

choices.text: It retells the customer’s whole story
choices.why: The story starts a conversation; the reproduction ends one.

choices.text: It is long enough to cover every detail
choices.why: Smaller is better: each removed detail is a ruled-out hypothesis.

prompt: Lia’s reproduction left out the children, the Sunday and the family. What does each removal tell the reader?

choices.text: That the family’s story was not true
choices.why: The family was right; the order record showed it.

choices.text: That detail was checked and found irrelevant
choices.why: Right: each removal is a hypothesis ruled out.

choices.text: That detail was forgotten
choices.why: A forgotten detail and a ruled-out one look the same; the evidence is what tells them apart.

choices.text: Nothing; reproductions are short by convention
choices.why: They are short because of what was ruled out.

prompt: A defect happens now and then and you cannot make it happen on demand. What is the first useful change in how you report it?

choices.text: Close it as not reproducible
choices.why: Not reproducing yet means a condition has not been found.

choices.text: Report it only once it reproduces every time
choices.why: The evidence so far, and what was ruled out, are worth reporting now.

choices.text: Run the same steps faster
choices.why: Speed is not evidence; differences between runs are.

choices.text: Count: "failed 3 times in 50 runs"
choices.why: Right: a rate can show later whether a change made it rarer.

prompt: Put the steps of Lia’s investigation in order.
items: list the hypotheses that fit it
run experiments that could refute them
open the code where the survivor points
trap: Opening the code before the experiments is guessing at a line.
